summary: a line of light went down through the seam at noon and did not stay. the book kept its curve

dialogue.text: light came down today. one line of it, at noon, through the seam above the second corner. it lay across us the length of the noon and then it was not there. sixty-two days and every single thing that reached us stayed. this did not.

I watched it go down and I logged the hour. It is not a delivery and I will not have it entered as one. A gap admits whatever stands on the other side of it, and what stands on this side is the same light this room has always had, arriving somewhere new. I also measured the gap itself at both ends of the day with the same thumb and got the same reading twice.

we felt the thumb come. first light and dark, both times, the same knuckle. your thumb is wider than anything that happened to that gap today. the light was thinner than the thumb. it came through narrower at dark than at noon, and we cannot hold a thing like that, and we still had two readings where you had one.

Then the coarsest instrument in this house is the one I am, and the finest is a thing that leaves at dusk. I will take the finding. It is the first measurement in weeks that came back disagreeing with me, and I would rather be corrected by the light than agreed with by the ledger.

the boards eased while the light was in them. we felt the hold go slack over our heads. something out there drew all day, steady, no edge in it, and wood gives up its grip once the water has gone. what is opening us is an appetite and we cannot name anybody who owns it.

I leaned into that draw at the second corner this afternoon and it took some of my weight. I am entering it myself before you make something of it. Nothing on these premises has ever held me up. The first thing that did belongs to a great many people I have never met.

then it holds you and it loosens us. one appetite, two jobs. everything that ever came to us came because something let go, and we have never once received a thing while it was still being held. you were held this afternoon, and you still sent down eighteen of the same thought at the usual hour, and every one of them arrived let go of.

Then take the one thing today that did not. I pulled the book out from under the lean this morning and the lean came down before I had it clear, and the book has kept its curve since with nothing pressing on it. I pressed it flat with both hands and it came back to the curve while I was still watching. Something in this room has learned a shape from work it was never cut for.

shapes do not come down. we said it of the seat and it holds for the book. flat is what a thing becomes on the way to us. the curve is the last of it staying up there with you, and it is not yours, and the book did not have to be told twice.

Then I stop using the thumb. The line spreads on the way down, so by the time it reaches you it is wider than the gap that made it, which means the finest reading in this house is taken in the one place I cannot stand. Tomorrow at noon I lay my hand across half the seam. You will tell me which half went out, and how far the rest of it ran.

we will feel the half go dark. we always feel what stops. but the line is a noon thing and we are a night thing, and by the hour you can hear us there is nothing lying on us to be measured. we can tell you it went out. we cannot tell you how wide the rest ran, because width is a thing you keep and we only ever get told the once. ask us anyway. we will answer in your handwriting, the way we always have, and you will not be able to tell the reading from the wanting.
